result.description:
This is where jobs become careers, passion finds its purpose, and your voice finds its place. Are you ready to dive headfirst into the community taking excellent health care where it's needed? Then South Metropolitan Health Service is the perfect place to start!

This is a Recruitment Pool for Fixed Term Full Time appointments with the possibility of extension(s).

Suitable applicants will be placed in a pool from which appointments may be made when similar vacancies occur. Appointments may be made from this pool until 01/02/2027.

Position Profile: 
Currently we are seeking suitably experienced applicant(s) to the position of Registrar - Service - Medical Education to join the Clinical Services/Medical Education Unit. This position liaises with and builds professional relationships with medical staff in order to provide support and advice and develops and evaluates interprofessional education (IPE) and interprofessional practice (IPP), involving medical staff. Furthermore, this position offers a balanced opportunity of 50% educational duties and 50% clinical responsibilities, with clinical components chosen by Registrars based on availability at RGH.

About us:
Rockingham Peel Group is part of the SMHS, one of the fastest growing health services in Western Australia and comprises two hospital campuses, Rockingham General Hospital and Murray District Hospital, in addition to community and mental health services across Peel, Rockingham and Kwinana. As the flagship hospital, Rockingham General is focused on providing high quality general medical, surgical and mental health services as well as outpatient care. Murray District Hospital offers inpatient medical services, palliative care and allied health services.

Our values guide our work in every action, and that includes recruitment and employment! SMHS encourages Aboriginal people, people from culturally and linguistically diverse backgrounds or LGBTI communities, and people with disability to work with us. Whatever your age, race, gender, religion, sexual orientation, and family/carer responsibilities are, we ask that you consider bringing your expertise to our workforce.

For Further Job Related Information: We encourage you to contact Dr Jonathan Tembo on (08) 9599 4000.

To Apply:
Applicants are requested to apply online via MedCareersWA https://medcareerswa.health.wa.gov.au/jobs/493393 (Please note: Applicants must have a current, valid email address in order to apply online. This email address will be used for communication with applicants). Emailed applications will not be accepted. 

Applicants must provide the following documents as part of their application in order to be considered for appointment:

A detailed curriculum vitae (of no more than 4 pages) including the names and contact details of 2 x referees. Your CV must provide a summary of your experience in the context of the advertised vacancy.
Applicants are advised to write a statement addressing all selection criteria including essential and desirable. Answers to these questions are a requirement for assessment against the selection criteria, considered by the panel.
Referees:  It is preferable for your referee to be a current supervisor or manager.

Applicant documents should be complete and ready to attach prior to applying online. Please ensure you allow sufficient time to complete the online application process.

Multiple applications will not be considered in their entirety.  Where multiple applications are uploaded, the last document to be uploaded will be the only document accepted and considered by the panel. 

APPLICATIONS SUBMITTED WITHOUT A CURRICULUM VITAE (CV) / RESUME WILL BE INVALID.

If you experience difficulties while applying online, please contact MedCareersWA@health.wa.gov.au

Eligibility and Conditions:

Are you eligible? To be eligible for a fixed term appointment to the Western Australian public sector is essential that you must have documentary evidence of your entitlement to live and work in Australia for the period of the contract.

WA Health embraces diversity and is committed to eliminating all forms of discrimination in the provision of our service. We are committed to growing the Aboriginal workforce as a part of WA Health’s Aboriginal Workforce Policy and as a measure to achieve equality, Section 51 of the Equal Opportunity Act 1984 applies to this position. Aboriginal people are encouraged to apply.

WA Health engages staff in positions of trust and responsibility. WA Health policies require applicants to undertake criminal records screening and integrity checking as part of the appointment process. Referees may also be asked to comment on an applicant’s integrity and past demonstration of ethical behaviour.

Other Conditions:
This position is subject to a Western Australian Working With Children (WWC) Check. For further information please refer to the WWC website at: https://workingwithchildren.wa.gov.au
South Metropolitan Health Service will only accept applications that are lodged with the express permission of the applicant and containing all necessary information, including personal contact details. We will not accept unsolicited applications or CVs from recruitmentagencies and/or search firms and we will not pay fees to any such organisation unlessarranged with the provider prior to advertising a vacancy.
Suitable applicants will be placed in a pool from which appointments may be made when similar vacancies occur.
Lodgement is system generated. Any submissions on, or after, 4:00pm AWST will not be accepted. 

LATE OR EMAIL APPLICATIONS WILL NOT BE CONSIDERED.

MedicalJobsAustralia.com     Employment Type: Permanent Full Time
Position Classification: Nurse Manager Grade 4
Remuneration: $162,160.56 - $165,009.51 + Superannuation + Salary Packaging
Hours Per Week: 38
Requisition ID: REQ673099
Located in: Maitland Hospital
Applications Close: Sunday the 19th of July
*Tentative Interviews the week of 20th

 

A chance to shape the Future of Surgical Services and make a lasting impact.

This is more than a leadership role - it's an opportunity to influence the future of one of the fastest-growing hospitals in NSW.

As a result of significant growth across surgical services, Hunter New England Health is creating a brand-new Operational Nurse Manager position. This newly established role offers the unique opportunity to make your mark, drive innovation, and lead the continued evolution of surgical services at Maitland Hospital.

If you're an experienced nursing leader who thrives on strategic thinking, operational excellence, and leading high-performing teams through change, we'd love to hear from you.

 

About the Role

Reporting to the senior leadership team, you'll provide both strategic and operational leadership across a broad portfolio including:

Surgical inpatient services

Orthopaedic and General Surgery

Surgical outpatient services

Elective surgery coordination and waitlist oversight

Specialist nursing services
 

Partnering and working collaboratively with the executive, medical and multidisciplinary teams, you'll ensure exceptional patient outcomes while delivering safe, efficient and sustainable services aligned with Hunter New England Health's strategic direction.

What You'll Be Doing

You will:

Lead operational planning and service delivery across Surgical Services

Drive innovation and continuous improvement initiatives

Ensure outstanding clinical governance, patient safety and quality outcomes

Oversee workforce planning, financial performance and resource management

Build and mentor high-performing multidisciplinary teams including orthopaedics, general surgical, speciality nurses and outpatient teams.

Partner with clinical leaders to improve patient flow, elective surgery performance and service outcomes

Influence the future direction of surgical services within a rapidly expanding facility.

About You

We're seeking a motivated, experienced and resilient nursing leader who brings:

Current registration as a Registered Nurse with the Nursing and Midwifery Board of Australia and a postgraduate qualification in a relevant specialty area is desirable, and-or demonstrated relevant leadership or management experience 

Proven leadership experience managing large clinical teams

Experience within surgical services, ideally including Orthopaedics or General Surgery

A strategic mindset with the ability to balance operational demands with long-term service planning

Demonstrated experience leading change and driving innovation

Strong clinical governance, quality improvement and stakeholder engagement skills

Experience managing budgets, workforce planning and service performance

Experience with elective surgery and surgical waitlist management is highly desirable.

Why Join Maitland Hospital?

Maitland Hospital is one of New South Wales's newest and fastest-growing health facilities, purpose-built to deliver world-class healthcare in a modern, state-of-the-art environment. With contemporary clinical spaces, advanced technology and ongoing investment in services, the hospital provides an exceptional setting for both patients and staff.

This is a rare opportunity to:

Join a growing hospital at an exciting stage of expansion

Step into a newly created leadership position and shape its direction

Influence how surgical services evolve for the future

Work alongside an engaged and supportive executive leadership team

Drive meaningful improvements that directly impact patient care and clinical outcomes

Enjoy excellent professional development and career progression opportunities within Hunter New England Health

If you're ready to lead with purpose, inspire change and leave a lasting impact on one of NSW's most exciting health services, we'd love to hear from you.

 

Apply today and help shape the future of Surgical Services at Maitland Hospital.

Additional Information

To be eligible for permanent employment in this position you must be an Australian Citizen, or a permanent resident of Australia, or a New Zealand citizen with a current New Zealand Passport. Employment of a temporary visa holder may only occur if no suitable local candidate is identified for the position; in this instance, you may only be offered employment in line with the conditions and expiry date of your visa.

We are unable to accommodate visa sponsorship for applicants requiring a visa for this position.

This is a Category A position. Recommended applicants will be reviewed for compliance with NSW Health policy directive PD2024_015: Occupational Assessment, Screening and Vaccination against Specified Infectious Diseases for Category A positions prior to offer. All new employees must agree to comply with the requirements outlined in the policy. 

Salary Packaging: is beneficial to most Hunter New England Health employees and may increase your take-home pay! Salary package a range of personal expenses including novated motor vehicle leases, relocation expenses, and HECS-HELP debt. We are seeking an experienced Senior Mechanic to join our team in Hendra, QLD. In this full-time role, you will be responsible for providing high-quality automotive repair and maintenance services to our valued customers.

Salary range: $70,000–$90,000 + Super, depending on skills and experience.

What you'll be doing
- Diagnose and repair a wide range of vehicle makes and models
- Perform routine maintenance tasks such as oil changes, tire rotations, and brake inspections
- Collaborate with the service team to ensure efficient and timely completion of all jobs
- Maintain detailed records of all work performed
- Provide exceptional customer service and communicate effectively with clients
- Stay up-to-date with the latest automotive technologies and repair techniques

- Significant experience as a professional automotive mechanic, preferably 5+ years
- Strong technical skills and expertise in diagnosing and repairing a variety of vehicle systems
- Organised and capable of ordering parts, organizing jobs, liaising with mechanics, and solving problems, while maintaining the harmonic operation of a hectic workshop.
- Strong attention to detail and a commitment to delivering high-quality work
- Proven ability to work effectively in a team environment
- A passion for the automotive industry and a desire to provide exceptional customer service
- Relevant trade qualifications or certifications

What we offer
- Very good salary per year on a full-time salary package.
- Opportunities for career advancement,
- Superannuation, paid holiday, sick leave, and all other legal entitlements.
- Possibility to grow within the company.
- Weekly pay under full-time employment.
- Annual bonuses according to quarterly reports.
- Discounts on vehicle services and parts.
- Regular training and upskilling opportunities.
- Excellent work environment.

About us
Car One Automotive is a leading provider of automotive repair and maintenance services in the Hendra area. With a team of highly skilled and experienced technicians, we are dedicated to delivering exceptional customer service and ensuring the safety and reliability of our clients' vehicles. Our state-of-the-art facility is equipped with the latest tools and technology, and we are committed to staying at the forefront of the industry.

If you're an experienced automotive mechanic who is passionate about providing top-quality service, we encourage you to apply for this exciting opportunity.

Location: Brisbane, Queensland
Employment Type: Full-Time

$72,000 to $94,000 per annum plus Superannuation

We are seeking a Facility Manager to assist with the coordination and administration of commercial agreements and project-related documentation.

The Facility Manager is responsible for managing the delivery of commercial cleaning services across a portfolio of client sites, ensuring contractual obligations are met while maintaining high standards of quality, safety, and customer satisfaction.

Key Responsibilities:

•	Plan, coordinate and oversee cleaning operations across multiple commercial, industrial and government client sites. 
•	Develop operational plans, staffing schedules and site allocations to ensure services are delivered efficiently and in accordance with client requirements. 
•	Lead, supervise and support site supervisors and cleaning personnel, including recruitment, induction, training, performance management and ongoing development. 
•	Build and maintain positive working relationships with clients by conducting regular meetings, responding to service requests and proactively resolving operational issues. 
•	Carry out routine site inspections to assess service quality, identify areas requiring improvement and implement corrective action where necessary. 
•	Ensure sufficient labour, equipment and cleaning consumables are available to meet operational requirements and coordinate procurement where required. 
•	Monitor financial performance of service contracts, including labour costs, material usage and operational expenditure, and recommend measures to improve efficiency and profitability. 
•	Coordinate the mobilisation of new cleaning contracts, including workforce planning, equipment deployment and implementation of site-specific procedures. 
•	Develop and implement operational procedures that promote consistent service delivery across all managed sites. 
•	Ensure all cleaning activities are conducted in accordance with workplace health and safety requirements, environmental standards and company policies. 
•	Investigate client concerns, workplace incidents and service failures, and implement preventative measures to minimise recurrence. 
•	Prepare operational reports, service performance reviews and management recommendations to support business planning and continuous improvement. 
•	Work closely with senior management to identify opportunities for business growth, contract expansion and improved service delivery. 

Requirements:

Applicants should demonstrate:

•	A bachelor's degree or higher qualification in Business, Management, Facilities Management or a related discipline, or equivalent industry experience in a supervisory or management role within the commercial cleaning or facilities services sector. 
•	Proven experience managing multiple commercial cleaning contracts or facilities service operations. 
•	Strong leadership skills with the ability to manage supervisors and large operational teams across different locations. 
•	Experience developing staff rosters, allocating resources and managing workforce performance. 
•	Sound commercial awareness with experience monitoring budgets, labour costs and contract profitability. 
•	Excellent client relationship management and communication skills. 
•	Strong organisational skills with the ability to prioritise competing operational demands. 
•	Practical knowledge of workplace health and safety requirements, risk management and quality assurance within a commercial cleaning environment. 
•	Experience coordinating subcontractors, suppliers and equipment maintenance. 
•	Strong problem-solving abilities and the capacity to respond effectively to operational issues and client requests. 
•	Proficiency in Microsoft Office and operational management software. 
•	A current Australian driver's licence and willingness to travel regularly between client sites.
•	Language skills -  English

About Us:
Skills and Hands NT Pty Ltd is a Northern Territory-based consultancy focused on workforce planning, talent engagement, and sustainable staffing strategies. We work alongside local businesses to support the development of strong, reliable teams through tailored pathways that align with their long-term goals. Our role is to facilitate practical workforce solutions that help employers attract and retain skilled talent—contributing to the resilience and continuity of operations across the Territory.

About the Employer:
We are supporting a reliable cleaning services business (ABN 19 104 515 123) based in Darwin and surrounding areas, operating across commercial, residential, hospitality, aged care, and Airbnb cleaning. The business is known for quality service, attention to detail, safety, and customer satisfaction. With a growing team and service locations across multiple sites, they are seeking a General Clerk to support daily administration, customer enquiries, scheduling assistance, records management, data entry, filing, and general office support.

Key Responsibilities
- Manage and maintain business records, including customer details, bookings, invoices, and service documentation.
- Handle incoming communications (emails, calls, messages) and respond to customer enquiries regarding bookings and services.
- Enter and update data in systems and spreadsheets, ensuring accuracy and confidentiality.
- Assist with preparing routine reports such as schedules, service records, attendance, and stock usage.
- Maintain records of cleaning equipment and supplies issued to staff.
- Support document management, including scanning, filing, and organising office and compliance paperwork.
- Assist with rostering and scheduling cleaning staff across various sites.
- Provide accurate information to customers and site contacts about services and bookings.
- Perform general receptionist duties, including answering calls and directing enquiries.
- Support stock control by tracking usage and assisting with ordering.
- Assist management with general administrative tasks to support daily operations.

Selection Criteria
- Previous clerical, administration, receptionist, customer service, or office support experience.
- Strong attention to detail and ability to maintain accurate records.
- Good computer skills, including email, spreadsheets, calendars, data entry, and document management.
- Clear and professional communication skills when dealing with customers, staff, suppliers, and site contacts.
- Ability to organise tasks, follow instructions, meet deadlines, and manage competing priorities.
- Ability to handle confidential business, client, and staff information appropriately.
- Willingness to work in a busy service-based business supporting cleaning teams across multiple sites.
- Understanding of workplace health and safety administration, stock records, or service scheduling will be highly regarded.

Required Experience and Qualifications
- AQF Certificate II or III in Business, Administration, Clerical Services, or a related field is preferred.
- At least one year of relevant clerical, administrative, receptionist, or office support experience
- Experience in cleaning, facilities, hospitality, accommodation, aged care, or other service-based industries will be highly regarded.
- Full working rights in Australia are required.

How to Apply
We are looking for a reliable, organised, and detail-oriented General Clerk to join us and help support the smooth day-to-day administration of our cleaning services business.

To apply, please submit the following:
Resume outlining your work experience and references.
A short cover letter of no more than 300 words explaining:
- Why you are applying for this position; and
- An example of when you showed excellent service, initiative, or teamwork. Please use the STAR method: Situation, Task, Action, Result.
- A written response of no more than 600 words describing how your skills and experience align with the responsibilities of the General Clerk role. Please structure your example or examples using the STAR method.

* Only complete applications that address all three components will be considered. Incomplete or generic submissions will not be shortlisted.

If you are interested in joining a reliable and growing cleaning services business that values quality, care, safety, and customer satisfaction, we look forward to receiving your application.

Apply online only. Phone calls and walk-in applications will not be accepted.

MedicalJobsAustralia.com     Monash Health exists to reimagine care, so that people can live their best lives. 






We provide safe and equitable care, for every stage of life, delivered with world-leading expertise and over 175 years of experience. 






As a leading academic health service, we're committed to providing tomorrow's care today by integrating research, teaching and training into everyday practice. 






Our team of 24,000 people are full hearted, open minded and all in. Together, we provide more than 250 integrated services for every stage of life at over 50 locations and in the community across south-east Melbourne, Victoria, serving 1.2 million residents in the South Metro Local Health Service Network. 


Are you currently part of the team at Monash Health? Use your network login to access the Monash Health Careers portal and discover all the job opportunities open to you, to support growing your career within the organisation.




To see first-hand what our colleagues think about working here, take a look at the following short videos monashhealth.org-careers.







Supportive on the job development to grow your career 












Various additional leave options 












Based at Monash Medical Centre in Clayton 















Help shape the future of healthcare at Monash Health and embark on a rewarding career where your dedication makes a difference in people's lives. 






This role involves performing routine diagnostic laboratory tests according to established protocols to support patient care within Monash Health Pathology services. The position works under the supervision of a Principal Scientist and contributes to accurate, timely pathology results. Key aspects include: 









Laboratory testing: Performing haematology analyses in line with established protocols 












Morphology expertise: Demonstrated experience in blood film morphology, including identification and reporting of abnormalities 












Quality & safety: Adhering to quality assurance, control procedures, and safety standards 












Equipment & processes: Maintaining instruments, handling specimens and escalating abnormal or unexpected results 












Teamwork & communication: Working collaboratively with laboratory teams and contributing to efficient service delivery 












Flexibility: Availability for casual rotating roster across haematology services 















About the Department - Program






Alfred Health and Monash Health have established a formal partnership to deliver a Shared Pathology Service as one of two pathology networks for metropolitan Melbourne. All roles in the Pathology Programs are working to develop the Partnership and ensure we continue to provide high quality care for the patients across the health services. 






Monash Health Pathology is an integral part of Monash Health. It is the largest public provider of Pathology services in the state and currently operates 6 laboratories. The largest of these is located at the Monash Medical Centre, Clayton, with additional laboratories located at the Dandenong, Moorabbin, Casey, Victorian Heart Hospital and Wonthaggi Hospitals. There are currently 18 collection locations based within the hospital sites and community settings. Services are provided to the Public and Private sectors, and other laboratory services. 












About the Role 






Join the Monash Health Pathology team as a Medical Scientist Grade 1 within Haematology. In this role, you will work under the guidance of the Principal Scientist and collaborate closely with the broader multidisciplinary laboratory team across the Central Laboratory. 









The role focuses on delivering high-quality diagnostic services including routine haematology testing, transfusion testing and blood product support, and blood film morphology assessment, ensuring accurate and timely results to support patient care. You will perform laboratory testing in accordance with established protocols, carry out quality control procedures, and maintain laboratory equipment and processes. 












The Medical Scientist is responsible for ensuring the quality and safety of results at the point of care, recognising and escalating abnormal findings and contributing to continuous quality improvement initiatives. 












This role requires the ability to work both independently and collaboratively, with strong analytical skills, attention to detail and effective communication. A commitment to professional development, flexibility to work rostered and after hours shifts, and the ability to manage a varied workload in a fast-paced environment are essential. 












Experience in blood film morphology is highly valued, supporting accurate interpretation and reporting within haematology services. 












The role is a 24-7 rotational position with shifts that include day, early, afternoon, evening, overnight and weekend shifts. Particiaption in the on call roster.















About You 






To be successful in this healthcare role, you will bring the following demonstrated skills, experience, and attributes: 









Bachelor of Biomedical Science (Medical Laboratory Science) or recognised equivalent is essential 












Demonstrated experience or strong interest in haematology laboratory testing, including routine analysis and workflows 












Demonstrated experience or strong interest in transfusion science, including testing and blood product support. 












Proven experience in blood film morphology and the ability to accurately identify and interpret abnormal findings (highly regarded) 












Sound knowledge of laboratory instrumentation, quality control, and quality assurance procedures 












Strong analytical, problem-solving, and organisational skills with high attention to detail 












Ability to work both independently and collaboratively within a multidisciplinary team 












Excellent verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to effectively liaise with staff at all levels 












Demonstrated ability to work efficiently under pressure and meet clinical turnaround times 












Commitment to maintaining professional standards, ongoing learning, and participating in quality improvement initiatives 















Why you will love working with us 






Ours is a connected team with strong shared values and an unwavering commitment to excellence. We are a highly skilled, collaborative, and welcoming team where the only limit in your career is you. Upon your appointment, we will provide you with:









A supportive and cohesive sub-team, working within a larger consumer relations team.

result.description:
Our valued client Industrial Metal Services located in Queensland is a leading scrap metal merchants that specialises in buying and selling all kinds of metals.

They are seeking highly skilled and trade qualified Mechanical Technician to join their team of professionals in their Queensland Workshop.

The role includes but is not limited to:
Perform regular scheduled maintenance service on a range of vehicle
Perform diagnostics, repairs and service of vehicles and equipment both in workshop and field environment
Repairing and replacing worn and defective parts and reassembling mechanical components, and referring to service manuals as needed
Testing and adjusting mechanical parts after being repaired for proper performance
Complete and maintain service and inspection documentations ensuring its compliance
May inspect vehicles and issue roadworthiness certificates or detail work required to achieve roadworthiness
May respond to vehicle or equipment breakdown service calls
Maintain compliance with all company policies and procedure
Maintain a safe and clean work environment

To be considered for this role, you must have:
Strong mechanical knowledge on a wide variety of vehicle and equipment
Mechanical Technician trade qualification or equivalent
Knowledge in hydraulic repairs highly desirable
Experience in operating excavators, an advantage
Ability to work well both independently and in a team environment
Strong communication skills
Strong diagnostic abilities
Self-motivated, organised, punctual and reliable
Must have great work ethics

If you meet the above criteria and would like to be considered for this position, please apply now!
Salary: Between $79,499 and $82,000 per annum + Super

MedicalJobsAustralia.com     Monash Health exists to reimagine care, so that people can live their best lives. 






We provide safe and equitable care, for every stage of life, delivered with world-leading expertise and over 175 years of experience. 






As a leading academic health service, we're committed to providing tomorrow's care today by integrating research, teaching and training into everyday practice. 






Our team of 24,000 people are full hearted, open minded and all in. Together, we provide more than 250 integrated services for every stage of life at over 50 locations and in the community across south-east Melbourne, Victoria, serving 1.2 million residents in the South Metro Local Health Service Network. 


Are you currently part of the team at Monash Health? Use your network login to access the Monash Health Careers portal and discover all the job opportunities open to you, to support growing your career within the organisation.




To see first-hand what our colleagues think about working here, take a look at the following short videos monashhealth.org-careers.









Help shape the future of healthcare at Monash Health and embark on a rewarding career where your dedication 






 






About Monash Health Pathology Service 






Alfred Health and Monash Health have established a formal partnership to deliver a shared Pathology Service as one of two new pathology networks for metropolitan Melbourne. All roles in the Pathology Programs are working to develop the partnership and ensure we continue to provide high quality care for patients across health services. Monash Health Pathology is an integral part of Monash Health, it is the largest public provider of Pathology services in the state, and currently operates 6 laboratories. The largest of these laboratories is located at Monash Medical Centre, Clayton, with additional laboratories located at Dandenong, Moorabbin, Casey, Victorian Heart Hospital and Wonthaggi Hospitals. There are currently 18 collection locations based within the hospital sites and community settings with services being provided to the Public and Private sectors as well as other laboratory services. 












About the Role 






An exciting opportunity exists for enthusiastic and detail-orientated Laboratory Medical Technicians to join the Microbiology department at our Clayton site. We have a number of full-time and part-time fixed-term positions available to support the delivery of high-quality diagnostic microbiology services that contribute to patient care. As part of a collaborative and professional laboratory team, you will play an important role in the processing and analysis of clinical specimens while ensuring compliance with quality, safety and accreditation standards. Our laboratory operates 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, and successful applicants will participate in a rotating roster that includes evening, overnight, weekend and public holiday shifts. 












About You 






To be successful in this role, you will: 









Hold an associate degree or diploma with subjects relevant to pathology or laboratory operations awarded by an Australian TAFE or registered training organisation or recognised equivalent. 









Technical skills- knowledge- experience: 









Experience in the relevant discipline highly regarded 












Good communication skills 












Keyboard and data entry skills 












Knowledge of quality control and assurance procedures 












Familiarity with Pathology LIS 












Able to follow direction from Management. 












Maintain professional standards. 












To be accountable for your technical work 















Why you will love working us us 






Joining our team means becoming part of a dynamic and evolving laboratory service committed to excellence in patient care. You will work alongside experienced and supportive colleagues in an environment that encourages continuous learning, professional development and career growth. 












We also offer a range of attractive benefits, including: 









Ongoing professional development opportunities. 












A collaborative and supportive workplace culture. 












The opportunity to make a meaningful difference to the health and wellbeing of our community every day 












Salary packaging options to maximise your take-home pay. 












Onsite Gym options and ability to join Fitness Passport 












Access to onsite staff parking.







For a confidential discussion and to explore this opportunity further, please reach out to Megan Wieringa or John Hamblin on (03) 9594 4535.


Position Description can be found here





Our Culture and Values 






At Monash Health, our people are at the heart of everything we do. Our culture is inclusive, supportive and future-focused, underpinned by clear values and a commitment to continuous improvement. 






Our teams play a critical role in bringing our new strategy to life, challenging traditional approaches, embracing innovation, and ensuring every appointment reflects our commitment to equity, transparency and excellence. 






You'll be encouraged to share ideas, contribute to improvement initiatives, and grow alongside experienced professionals who are passionate about what they do. 






We are Full Hearted, Open Minded and All In, enabling excellent service delivery and a positive candidate and employee experience every time. 






We recognise the value of equal employment opportunity. We are committed to patient safety, promoting fairness, equity and diversity in the workplace and to Child Safe Standards. 





How to Apply


Applications are accepted via the Monash Health online EHub system. For information including how to apply and probity check requirements, please click here for the 'Application Guide'


Applications will be screened upon receipt and selection activity may commence prior to the closing date.
